newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front - March 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front - March 20.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on Thursday:
WASHINGTON - President Clinton nominated George Tenet, who has been deputy CIA director since 1995, to head the spy agency and predicted he would win easy Senate confirmation.

WASHINGTON - The CIA is investigating whether a senior officer in the agency's elite clandestine service arranged for a favorable intelligence report on a major Democratic Party donor to be sent to the White House so that the man could attend events with President Clinton.

WASHINGTON - Mounting anti-Chinese sentiment in Washington is starting to affect U.S. policy toward Beijing in a host of areas, ranging from global trade negotiations to the Chinese lease of a former Navy base to the goals of Vice President Gore's upcoming trip to Beijing.
WASHINGTON - American Airlines and the Allied Pilots Association said they have reached a tentative agreement on a new contract that would end the threat of a late April strike.
WASHINGTON - William de Kooning, 92, one of the leading American artists of this century and a giant of abstract impressionism, died at his studio in East Hampton, New York.
WASHINGTON - After years of contentious debate, the Presbyterian Church (U.S.A.) has voted to require that all unmarried ministers, deacons and elders be sexually celibate.
WASHINGTON - The National Rifle Assciation is campaigning to persuade Virginia Gov. George Allen to veto a bill that would bar guns, knives and other weapons from Fairfax County's recreation centers.
